sections.heading: Why wool, and why the shrinkage
sections.html:
Wool quilts warm, quilts easily without a scrim, and drapes the way cotton wishes it could. Ours is needle-punched to the loft on the label, so it holds a hand without basting glue and never needs pre-soaking.

The label says it shrinks three to five percent when washed, because it does, and that puckered look is the reason your grandmother's quilts feel like your grandmother's quilts. If you want flat, we will tell you which of our blends stays flat and which shop sells it.

items.quote: The queen roll quilts like butter on the longarm and my customers ask for it by name now.

sections.heading: The washing question
sections.html:
Wash a wool quilt gently: cold water, mild soap, and the gentlest cycle the machine owns, or the bathtub if the quilt matters. Dry it flat or low, never wrung. The three to five percent shrink is the wool relaxing into the stitches, and it happens once.

For storage, fold along new lines a few times a year or keep it on a bed. Wool prefers being used; cedar chests and plastic bins are where quilts go to get musty.

items.a: Our carded wool is low-bearding by fleece selection, and the tighter your weave the less it travels. We swap the first roll if a loft fights your fabric.

items.q: Can it be machine quilted densely?
items.a: Yes. The needle-punch holds, and dense quilting on wool makes the softest stiff, which is a compliment in this building.
The sheep are range-raised on the farm and two partner ranches; the mill runs on the roof solar since 2021. Ask for the lot card and we will tell you which pasture.

sections.title: About the mill
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: The carder has been running since Eisenhower, outlived two roofs, and still sets the pace of the week.

sections.html:
The mill started because a wool grower's wife got tired of sending good fleece away and getting mediocre batting back. The carder was bought secondhand from a defunct mill in Ohio, trucked home on a flatbed, and has carded every roll since, including the ones your quilts are sleeping under.

Three generations later the flock is smaller and the loft standards are stricter. The carding room door still sticks in July, and the family still answers the phone, which is why wholesale accounts get a person and not a portal.

items.quote: They told me on the phone which roll would shrink the way my customer wanted. Who else knows their product like that?
items.author: A quilt shop owner

sections.heading: The terms, plainly
sections.html: Net thirty after the first order, no order minimum after the initial case, and a mill-store discount for the drive-in trade. Guild bulk buys ride the wholesale rate with one invoice and one very tall stack of rolls.
